title: Harden runtime preview ContextMenu scheduler lifecycle
description: `CreatureRuntimePreview.Generate()` is exposed through `[ContextMenu("Generate Creature")]`, but `_generationScheduler` is initialized only in `Awake()`. A manual edit-time ContextMenu invocation therefore deserves an explicit lifecycle contract: either ensure the scheduler is initialized before any public/manual Generate entry point, or explicitly prohibit ContextMenu generation outside a valid lifecycle and report a clear diagnostic. Verify how Unity invokes ContextMenu methods in the supported project workflow, add focused editor/manual coverage for the chosen contract, and preserve scheduler disposal/OnDestroy ownership. Do not create a second generation-scheduler abstraction; this is a narrow entry-point lifecycle hardening task.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Audit evidence 2026-09-11: current source has `[ContextMenu("Generate Creature")] public void Generate()` and `_generationScheduler = new CreatureGenerationScheduler()` only in `Awake()`. Static source inspection cannot prove Unity's exact edit-time invocation lifecycle, so this ticket records the boundary as a verification/hardening item rather than asserting a confirmed runtime defect. No source code was changed during the audit.
